title: The past, present, and future share a show floor at Pinball Expo 2026
gist: At Pinball Expo 2026, Stern controls roughly 90 percent of the pinball market while challengers, modular platforms like Multimorphic's P3 and free SDKs and browser tools are lowering barriers for homebrew designers. The author sees the sector's resurgence broadening geographically and in participants.

insights.claim: Stern's George Gomez says Stern controls 90 percent of the current pinball market at any given time, with everyone else splitting the rest.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: This is a company-insider estimate and not audited, but indicates one dominant licensor with a long tail of challengers.
insights.quote: “at any given time, Stern controls 90 percent of the current pinball market, and everybody else splits the rest.”

insights.claim: Challengers are growing beyond Chicago, including Texas-based Barrels of Fun and European producers like Dutch Pinball, and each year of the expo brings new companies.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Manufacturing is decentralizing, which suggests lower entry costs.

insights.claim: Multimorphic's P3 puts a ball-tracking interactive display in the lower two-thirds and a swappable upper playfield, with ten playfields and 30 games including software-only titles, addressing boredom with a $10,000 machine.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Swappable content converts a one-time hardware sale into a platform with recurring software and kit revenue.
insights.quote: “The way the P3 is designed is that the lower two-thirds is a ball-tracking interactive display…

insights.claim: Multimorphic offers a free SDK and says it is the only third-party development platform in pinball, with distribution through its own store to P3 owners.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: A controlled store on open tooling is the app-store model applied to physical entertainment.

insights.claim: Multimorphic's Dungeon Crawler Carl machine, with seven playable books, goes into production at year-end for early-next-year delivery, showing licensed IP driving the modular platform.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Franchise IP with strong fan bases is the demand driver for premium machines.

insights.claim: Johnny Zen's closed-beta browser-based Pinball Construction Set and the Pocket Pinball Android app let users design and play Visual Pinball X tables without CAD or a PC, with a planned artist marketplace.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Software tooling is pulling in a new cohort of designers, though it is early and unproven commercially.
insights.locator: Pocket Pinball and pinball construction set

insights.claim: Homebrew machines function as playable resumes that let hobbyists work without licensing restrictions, and some turn basement builds into careers with major manufacturers.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: A visible talent pipeline lowers hiring risk for incumbents and supports industry growth.

insights.claim: VR pinball with physical controls was seen as a novelty, with expo lines suggesting most people still prefer physical machines.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Physical tactility remains the core value, limiting the digital-substitution thesis.
